dialogues.content:
Where campfire light meets water, daffodils bloom.
A woman studies her rippling reflection — captivating enough to make the night sky pause in wonder.

"My beloved, where do you wander?"
"I've searched all Atlasia — through Luca's azure isles and Huaxu's emerald vales, where Aethyrie's breezes linger in the treetops, and where the Askard Fjord spring cracks the thinning ice."

"Yet I've found no one to cherish."
"The beauty who equals me must be imprisoned in the Sacred Lake of Elysium."
She murmurs softly to her own reflection.

options.content: Try to pick a daffodil from the lake

dialogues.content:
"Who are you? A passing traveler?"
She lifts her gaze, studying you with a fleeting glance.
"Come back when you've learned how to set her free."

In the distance, a lone old man tirelessly swings his hammer beside a mountain of discarded weapons.
One blow brings utter stillness,
the next ignites dancing firelights across the forge.
You approach, but the old man keeps his eyes fixed on his work.

"Another fool comes to die."
"Tell me, what year is it now?"

You open your mouth to answer— but wait.
What year is it now? What year should it be?
In the endless dark, you lost all measure of time long ago.
Your silence answers for you.

"So you're no different," he sighs.
"I stopped counting how many years I've been trapped here. The memories are gone — all that's left is this hammer, and the wrinkles time carved into me."
"While the fire still burns… speak. What is it you want?"

options.content: Choose a weapon from the pile.
Ask him to forge a weapon for you.

dialogues.content:
A song rises beside the lonely campfire.
A woman approaches—her steps light as feathers, her voice clear as a nightingale's call.

A leaden drowsiness creeps over you.
The darkness before your eyes crumples like parchment, dissolving in water.
 ……

You wander through sunlit woods and streams.
Water murmurs across velvet grass, while sunlight spills through the dense canopy in golden shafts.
Snow-white flying squirrels gently sip dawn dew. Azure lynxes and pale hares do not startle at your footsteps, they simply go about their business.

You sit in a tavern at dusk.
A bard plays his accordion as returning sailors clap and raise their voices in harmony.
Amid salty sea winds and sweet malt ale, you step into the heart of the crowd and dance—your feet light, your heart lighter.

You kneel beneath the sacred hall's stained glass.
The white-robed goddess gazes down from her towering portrait — serene, silent, and sorrowful.
The lunar deity steps forth from the mosaic's kaleidoscope hues, her beaded crown brushing your cheek as she kisses your forehead……

THWACK!
A sharp flick to your forehead snaps you out of sleep.
"I am the best Dreamweaver in Elysium! I work my fingers to the bone crafting perfect dreams, and you just lie there snoring? At least throw me a coin!"

"Up! Now!"
She snaps, flicking your forehead again in frustration.
An old man approaches the campfire. You notice he's carrying a lantern.

"Let me see… Oh! So you have a lantern too!"
"Yet all flames must fade in time. You know this — without light in the abyss, darkness claims you forever."
dialogues.speakerName: The Old Man with a Lantern

dialogues.content: "Best carry a spare lantern. Even the faintest glow may save your life on the road ahead."
dialogues.speakerName: The Old Man with a Lantern

options.content: Ask if he has other useful items

dialogues.content:
"Ah… Such generosity, traveler! May the God of Stars smile upon you on your path."
Every wrinkle on his face dances with delight.
dialogues.speakerName: The Old Man with a Lantern

dialogues.content:
"Ah… Such generosity, traveler! May the God of Stars smile upon you on your path."
Every wrinkle on his face dances with delight.
dialogues.speakerName: The Old Man with a Lantern

dialogues.content:
"Oh… My gracious. May the God of Abundance bless you, lest you remain this desperate — risking life over mere coins."
He grumbles away.
dialogues.speakerName: The Old Man with a Lantern

dialogues.content: "Wayward soul, the gods shall light your way."

A chorus of children's voices blooms in your mind. The campfire's glow dissolves into radiant light as your body grows weightless.
You float amidst a thousand whispering winds—cotton clouds brushing your fingertips, while golden towers pierce the clouds, their radiant silhouettes humming with silent invitation.
"Come. Receive the gods' grace and ascend beyond the clouds. The mortal realm fades beneath you; perfect bliss awaits."

You understand that every blessing from the heavens comes with a price.
You trust the path you tread with your own steps to empty promises of paradise.

The clouds cradle you gently like a mother's embrace.
Golden gates swing wide—just long enough to glimpse gods' shadows moving beyond. Then the clouds dissipate, depositing you back onto familiar soil.

You stretch toward the sky into that cottony illusion—pain licks up from your fingers like wildfire.
Light vanishes. Wind screams past as you plummet.
Of course. The abyss has no sky.

The figure draws near—
a girl, barely taller than a child with a fragile frame.

"May I… just… warm myself… by your fire?"
Her voice trembles. Water droplets roll from her soaked dress.
"I can't find my mom… It's freezing here… Please, let me sit by your fire! Just for a few minutes… I'll be…"

"Th-thank you."
Her voice trembles as the words slip through chattering teeth.
"I'm… I'm sorry… I didn't mean to bother you."
Ask her why she's here
Shaking, the girl disappears from view. Nothing is left but the flickering campfire, like she was never here at all.

"Why… why am I… That's right…"
"Dad… Mom… They're… Hyperboreans… We fled… trying to reach… Elysium…"
"At the sea… Our ship… swallowed by… a swirling black hole…"
The swirling black hole — you know it by its name. It's the black tide, the ravenous abyss that devours all substance.
Ask why her family risked going to Elysium

"Mon said… we were Demon's Children…"
"Even falling into the abyss… would be better… than staying in Hyperborea…"
"Thank you for the fire… and for letting me know… I'm already gone."
She vanishes. Nothing is left but the flickering campfire, like she was never here at all.
"Hey there!"
A cheerful young man with a backpack walks up to the campfire and greets you loudly.
"Don't mean to be blunt — but you're alive, right?"
"Never thought I'd meet another living soul out here! Guess we're both the lucky ones, huh?"

"Are you passed out?"
He crouches down, testing for breath.
"Don't tell me you're… one of the souls too?"

"Dad and I wrote a little folk song when I was 16. Apparently, the Hall of Divine Judgment didn't appreciate our lyrics."
"I should've been executed like my poor dad — until lightning struck the executioner on the very day."

You remain silent.
He sets down his backpack and pulls out water and food.

"At 20, I joined a band of traveling merchants. We were ambushed in a forest up in the North — tied up and abandoned in a cavern."
"I watched my companions starve to death one by one until dawn on the seventh day when a snuffling boar rooted me awake. A girl gave me some food. Pretty sure I was looking at an angel."
"Here, for you, my poor friend! May the first light over the sacred tower find you awake and well again."

"Later I traveled with a group of Knights into the abyss as a merchant. Their lights died one after another. An elder Knight tripped and found his sword buried in his own neck. I was the only one who survived."
"That was when I knew the Goddess of Fate had my back. That she would bless me with boundless luck and happiness."

"If she led me here, there must be something truly one-of-a-kind waiting in the depths. I won't keep it waiting."
He puts on his heavy backpack.

"Listen, my friend! If she spared you as well, then destiny has something wonderful in store just for you!"
He laughs, pumping his fists.
"To our good fortune!"

Two blood-red flowers, entwined at the stem, pulse with an eerie radiance.
You raise your lantern — its light spills over strands of faded blonde hair and segments of pallid vertebrae. Is this a Filthoid wearing human skin… or a man on the verge of becoming one?
You tense, grip tightening around your weapon — yet it makes no move to strike. Only those crimson eyes, set deep in shadow, watch you in silence.
Suddenly, its throat emits a fractured sound — like jagged stones grinding together, yet pulsing with strange rhythm. Against all reason, you comprehend the meaning—
"Please stay a moment, traveler with the lantern. Pray tell, do I still look beautiful in your light?"

"I braided my hair soft and shining, weaving beauty into every strand." Its fingers traced the ruptured flesh at the back of its head.
"I pressed my gown to perfection, adorned it with jewels fit for a queen." Its fingers brushed where crystal spikes tore through the flesh.
"I wear the necklace my lover gave me, to honor his devotion." Its fingers lingered over the jagged bones rising from its throat."
Those crimson eyes quiver ever so slightly, like petals trembling in the wind.
The crimson eyes are covered by savage claws.

"Thank you, kind traveler. Please accept a token of my gratitude."
"If you cross paths with my love, please tell him I'll always love him."

"No! My beloved must not see me in this wretched form."
"Please put me out of my misery, merciful traveler."
"Greetings, wandering stranger."
A finely-dressed young man pauses in the flickering firelight, offering you a graceful bow.
"I'm seeking a lady with crimson eyes. Have you glimpsed her passing?"

"She sings with such grace, even the nightingale falls silent in envy."
"Her golden hair flows like liquid sunlight, brighter than spring marigolds in bloom."
"She wears a gown of regal elegance, embroidered with jewels that shimmer like the night sky."
"And around her neck rests my gift — a crimson pendant, deep and mysterious as her gaze."
You haven't seen a lady like that.

"I see…"
His gaze falters briefly—just a moment — before composure returns.
"That's fine. My search continues."
The young man settles by the campfire, flames dancing in his untainted eyes.

"We were betrothed — she to be my bride upon her coming of age. Yet the gods marked her: a sacred sigil bloomed upon her brow. On the eve of her fourteenth birthday, their envoys spirited her away."
"Her parting words begged me to move on. But my vow stands eternal — this life belongs to her alone."
"When I find her, I'll bring her back to the world. The God of Full Moon, the patron of lovers, will surely bless our reunion."

options.content: Wish him luck in finding his lover.

dialogues.content:
"My gratitude, kind traveler."
"Please accept this humble gift — may fortune smile upon your own desires."

A faint smile touches his lips.
"Then I shall surrender this flesh to the Sacred Lake — that my soul may dwell eternally where hers resides."
A woman emerges by the campfire. She reaches her left hand into the flames, gathers soot, and scrawls unrecognizable symbols across the ground.

"Ah— time-defiant traveler, you who walk with despair, death clings to your shadow like a second skin."
She whispers.

"Ah, my dear friend. As you see, I am a poet."
"My quill now births its thousand-and-first child: your very own ode!"
She giggles.
The poet reaches into the fire again, slender fingers weaving through flames like a performer's nimble feet.

"My dear, behold—"
She spreads her pale hand before you — no blisters, no scars.
"A wise traveler like yourself must've known this is no true flame, and I am no mortal soul."

"What a wondrous place, don't you think?"
"Freed at last from flesh's torment, no mundane distractions to dull my inspiration. I am boundless now… I wield eternity!"
"Traveler, my gratitude for your pause — your presence kindles inspiration's spark. Take these verses, and may they guide you beyond the wheel of fate to your heart's desire."

The poet reaches out — embers surge like a tempest, swallowing your vision whole.
When the ash settles, only silence remains.
"Good day, Sir. May I share your fire's warmth?"

The boy approaches with exaggerated dignity, his steps still betraying youthful clumsiness.
He settles by the fire, nearly swallowed by an oversized formal coat that makes his slender frame seem even frailer. Holding a slender book up to the firelight, he begins reciting with solemn gravitas.
"God of Flames, grant us wisdom… God of Waters, bless our harvests…"

"Just… something my brothers gave me." He scratched his head with an embarrassed smile. "I need to get smarter before I stand before the gods."
"I was always the slow one in our family. My brothers were better at everything… But for some reason, the gods picked me instead. Nobody understands why."
"My brothers gave me this hymn book. They said I have to study really hard before meeting the Great Nine. 'Don't embarrass us,' they told me."
The boy scoots closer to you and lifts his book in a silent offer.
"Will you read it with me?"

You lean in. The moment your eyes meet the page, your blood turns to ice. Someone has scrawled the pages thick with ink-black, vile words.
The letters twist into black, barbed thorns, lashing around your limbs like starving serpents. Darkness creeps at the edges of your vision, swallowing the firelight whole.
Your body moves before your mind catches up, wrenching backward to tear your gaze from the cursed page.
You are not here to study books.

"Hey… are you okay? Did you see something scary?"
He tilts his head, eyes wide with innocent confusion.

"Oh, okay, I'll read it by myself then…"
He puts the book back onto his lap.

You open your mouth but no words come out.
The black thorns engulf the boy, swallowing him whole — until the boy, the book, and the thorns vanish into the void.

Suddenly, writhing black thorns burst from its pages.
Before you can react, the black thorns engulf the boy, swallowing him whole — until the boy, the book, and the thorns vanish into the void.
A middle-aged woman settles by the campfire, her grim expression untouched by the flickering light.
"Greetings, stranger. Pardon my asking, what is this place?"
Tell her

"Sacred lake…? Abyss…?" Her voice wavers with confusion. "These words mean nothing to me…"
She stares at her weathered hands. "I can't remember why I'm here."

options.content: Tell her about the history of the Sacred Lake

dialogues.content:
"People bearing sacred sigils… will be brought here…?"
"Ah… I remember now. My child is here. The sacred sigil appeared at the corner of her eye — like a butterfly about to take flight."

"Good idea."
She reaches into her pocket, pulling out a silver brooch.
She looks up. The firelight now burns clearly in her eyes.
"Ah… I remember now." She gently buffs the brooch with her sleeve. "This… this is meant for my child."

"I came for my child."
"They took her while she slept when I was not home. My girl's always feared strangers… If she wakes to unfamiliar faces—"
"I need to be with her… Yes. That's why I'm here."
"When did they take her?"
"Ten days ago… no, ten months… or is it ten years… Ah… I can't recall."

Her voice trails off. Now she sits transfixed, a statue with unblinking eyes and a seemingly unmoving chest.
Her mind has gone to a place where your voice can't reach.

"Crackle—"
The flames leap higher in an instant.
You see a golden-haired girl standing before the fire, her skirt lifted to cradle a handful of golden rocks. She drops them one by one into the flames.
The flames leap higher and higher, surging with the wild abandon of a forest greeting its first spring.

options.content: Ask the girl where she got the rocks

dialogues.content: "I know!" Her voice burns with passion, "How wonderful that we share the same view!"
"I picked these up around here," she says. "I think they're some kind of fire-magic crystal."
The girl keeps tossing the rocks. Maybe it's your imagination, but the flames seem to drift closer, gently caressing her golden hair.

"Come morning, the flames will be as they were, and these rocks will scatter around here once more."
"So every day, I gather and toss them into the flames again. Exactly one hundred forty-six of them."
"What's the point of this then?"
The girl tilts her head, blinking with an innocent smile.

"No, I love fire," she says. "I love its crackling sound, its dancing light."
"You see, space twists here. You close your eyes by the campfire and wake up at the bottom of the lake."
"But these little rocks are different — no matter how the world shifts, they always return. Just knowing I'll find them tomorrow lets me sleep in peace."
"Certainty comforts me."

The girl tosses her last rock.
The blaze embraces her, golden hair dissolving into its molten embrace.
"Mmm… Ugh…"
Feeble moans rise from the ground. You spot a skeleton of a man collapsing near the firepit, his hollow cheeks speaking of starvation.

"…Thank you for the kindness, kid. But my body's past eating."
"The black tide dragged me under. All the bread in the world couldn't save me now."
"You remind me of a little girl in Elysium… A child as kind-hearted as you."

Your heart aches at his state, yet your pack holds barely enough for yourself.
In this perilous abyss, survival comes first.

"She had golden locks, riding a giant pink boar. When I was starving on the streets, she offered me a piece of bread…"
"But my pride ran too deep. I refused the Elysian Church's charity and spat venom at her kindness."

"Now, looking back… I realise she might have been the only one who truly cared."
"Faith, race, birth… People use these things to embellish themselves… But no title can outshine the radiance of genuine kindness…"
"If I could go back… I'd kneel to beg her forgiveness… I don't think I have the chance now…"

His voice fades into whispers. You blink — and he's gone.
The scent of fresh-baked bread lingers in the air.

A golden light flashes — for a moment, you mistake it for dawn. Then you see it: a radiant bird, gliding down to land gracefully beside you.
Its feathers gleam like firelit gold, finer than any noble's treasure.

options.content: Pluck a feather from its tail
Pluck a feather from its head

dialogues.content: You pour water into your palm and offer it to the bird.
You reach quietly, plucking a golden tail feather while the bird rests. Its luster rivals the finest gold, priceless beyond measure.

Your fingers creep toward its head — but the bird snaps alert, eyes flashing open before you can strike.
The bird shrieks in fury, wings flaring as it dives. Its beak strikes like molten gold — searing a crimson brand into the palm of your hand.

It tilts its head, watching warily — then, with regal grace, dips its golden beak to sip.
With a grateful trill, it shakes its radiant feathers and takes flight—a golden spiral into the sky.
The bird shrieks in fury, wings flaring as it dives. Its beak strikes like molten gold — searing a crimson brand into the palm of your hand.
By the time the pain fades, the last glint of gold has long disappeared into the clouds.
By the time the pain fades, the last glint of gold has long disappeared into the clouds.

A putrid stench and reek of decay cut the air near you.
You see a girl emerge by the campfire. Her face and arms fester with weeping sores. Only the fire's reflection in her eyes betrays a flicker of life — without it, she might as well be a corpse.

options.content: You rummage through your backpack and offer the girl medicine.

dialogues.content:
"Thank you… kind traveler…"
Her head lifts slowly. You can't tell if that twisted smile is gratitude or just a grimace of pain.
You cautiously approach the girl, trying to assess her wounds.
Every nerve tenses at the sight of her symptoms. You get up and retreat, putting distance between you and the coughing girl.

"But please… Don't help me," she murmurs. "The Priest said this curse — this abyssal sickness — is my punishment…"
"I must repent sincerely… Then I'll get better… Until then, I must stay away from everyone."

"Cough…!"
She coughs violently—dark crimson blood spatters your outstretched hand, curling into ominous black mist.
"My apologies… for startling you… I-I'll leave right now…"
The girl staggers to her feet and vanishes into the darkness.

"I-I'm sorry…!"
She staggers upright and tries to retreat, but collapses back to the ground.
The girl staggers to her feet and vanishes into the darkness.

"The Priest said this curse — this abyssal sickness — is my punishment…"
"I must repent sincerely… Then I'll get better… Until then, I must stay away from everyone."
The girl struggles up once more, then stumbles away into the swallowing dark.

You settle by the campfire, resting the lantern at your feet.
The moment your fingers release it, water surges across the ground. Before you can react, a whirlpool drags the lantern into the depths.

A figure in a ridiculous bird mask emerges waist-deep from the water and shakes his head with a splash. He spreads his arms wide and summons three lanterns above the water — identical in form yet made from different materials.
"Greetings, dear traveler! Pray tell — did you drop this golden lantern, this humble wooden lantern, or perhaps… this perfectly ordinary lantern?"

"Ahahaha!" His whole body shakes from the laughter. "Splendid! I like your style! True greed doesn't ask — it takes!"
"Take it, darling! Who could resist such glittering gold — am I right?!"

"Hmm? You… intrigue me!" He tilts his head, his dark eyes bottomless. "Wood makes for poor lanterns — yet why shouldn't it? This is the abyss! Everything's possible here!"
"Blessings upon you, dear one! What an interesting journey awaits."
Tsk, tsk, the Elysian Church has turned you all into such dull people. He sighs dramatically, disapproving of your choice. "Honesty is so dreadfully dull. Don't you want a new lantern?"

The man plunges into the water, and the surface vanishes without a trace.
The lantern sits undisturbed at your feet, while scattered embers litter the ground around it.

The man plunges into the water, and the surface vanishes without a trace.
The lantern sits undisturbed at your feet, yet beside it now rests an Artefact.
"Very well." He shakes his head. "Honesty is supposed to be a virtue, isn't it? Then let the tale unfold — here's your reward, just as the story promised."

The man plunges into the water, and the surface vanishes without a trace.
The lantern sits undisturbed at your feet, yet it burns brighter.

You hear the clash of metal upon metal.
Following the sound, you find the old man at a makeshift forge, hammer swinging with vigour. Sparks leap into the campfire's glow as sweat trickles down his brow.

"Ah, greetings, young one!" 
The old man calls out with cheerful warmth.
"Looks like you're trapped here too?" He gestures at himself with a wry smile. "So am I."
"Again? We've met before?" he asks, puzzled. "I can't seem to recall... My memory's not what it used to be..."

"It's not safe round here. I've forged a few weapons — feel free to take one." 
He gestures heartily toward his work. 
"Since I can't find a way out, I thought I'd return to my craft. Who knows — perhaps one day, one of these blades will find its way to a worthy knight, and they might lead us out of this wretched place."

options.content: Choose from the newly forged weapons.
Choose from the neatly arranged finished pieces.
Choose from the dusty corner of the forge.

dialogues.content: With your chosen weapon in hand, you set off once more, the old man's warm farewell echoing behind you.

Firelight falls across the withered face of an old man.
An iron hammer rests in his hand, and at his feet lie weapons, scattered across the earth.
At the sight of you, a faint spark of joy kindles in his eyes.

"Young one... do you know the road to Elysium?"
His voice is rough, brittle, worn thin by age.
"I have wandered these paths in circles, yet no matter how I search, I cannot find the road that leads me home..."

"I see... you too are lost, are you not?" 
The old man sighs deeply, bowing his head.

options.content: Ask if he might spare you a weapon.

dialogues.content:
"A weapon? You mean those scattered on the ground?"
"Ah... yes... I remember now. I was... a blacksmith."
"I forged arms for a few souls, helped them flee... and after that—"

His gaze clouds, as though he has finally remembered why he came to this place.
Then, with a faint shake of the head, he gives you a weary smile.

"Of course, child." 
"Take your pick. May it guard you well."

options.content: Choose from the weapons to his left.
Choose from the weapons to his right.

dialogues.content:
You tuck the weapon away. 
The old man seems to have forgotten you. His gaze lingers on the hammer in his hands, as though lost in solemn reflection.

The campfire flickers, etching the poet's downcast profile in shifting light.
She half-kneels by the fire, tracing winding patterns in the ash with her fingertip.

"If there is nowhere left to run, then embrace your fate."
"If words cannot become blades to pierce through lies, then let them be bricks with which to build our dreams—"
The poet pauses, lifting her finger slightly.
"Hmm..."

A memory stirs within your mind — you are certain you have heard this poem before.
A wisp of ash brushes your cheek, and almost without thinking, you whisper the missing final line:

options.content: "To write a lie, and kindle a flame that never dies."

dialogues.content:
"Hmm...!?" 
The poet lifts her gaze, astonishment softening into joy. 
"What a marvellous turn of phrase — just the ending I had longed for! How fortunate, to find a kindred spirit here."

options.content: "It was you who wrote it — in another time."

dialogues.content:
"'Another time'...?" 
At first she looks surprised, then her eyes brighten, kindled like the firelight itself. 
"Ah... So you are the one — the heart of this poem. The one I shall meet again, upon another path through time... is that it?"

"Then tell me — who truly wrote this poem, you or I? Heh... What a beguiling paradox... The Sacred Tree Scholars would be enthralled by such a tale."
The poet chuckles.
"When next we meet, allow me to write you a verse of your own. For now — give me your hand, that I might leave you with my blessing."

With the last of the ash upon her fingertip, the poet inscribes something upon your palm.
You cannot read the symbols, but their warmth feels vivid and ardent — and yet not burning in the least.
When you look up again, she is gone.

"O fickle God of Fate... At times Thou grantest joy, at times castest down in woe..." 
"Yet still we cleave to reverence... For Thy thread of purest white shall, in the end, bind us to the bliss of the Heaven above Heavens..." 
The boy recites with solemn devotion, wholly unaware of your presence.

You draw nearer, stealing a glance at the book in his hands.
Just as you remembered, the hymnal pages are defaced with writhing black script steeped in malice — as though straining to tear itself free of the page.

"Hello... are you here to read as well?" 
At last he notices you, lifting his head in quiet curiosity.
You pull the book from his hands and snap it shut.

You know, in your heart, that whatever you do now will not change what awaits him.
There is a greater task before you: to gather Glazeystal, and bring this long nightmare to an end.

"What are you—!?" 
He exclaims, worry creasing his brow. Then, staring at his empty hands, his voice drops to a murmur.
"Wait... I don't have to read anymore? I... I'm free?"

In the blink of an eye, black thistles surge forth, swallowing the boy whole. 
You let out a soft sigh... and press onward.

You suppress the pain prickling at your fingertips, and offer a faint smile. Then, you hurl the book into the fire.
The flames roar skyward — black thistles rising with them, lashing upward like a storm.

"My child... quick — look, there's a fire here." 
On the far side of the flames, a lone woman lifts her head and smiles. The firelight reveals the gaunt contours of her face.
"So warm... Thank you, kind stranger."
"My child is right here — see?"

You follow her gaze to a moss-covered stone, about waist height.
Set into a crevice near its crown, a glittering brooch gleams, ringed with delicate moss — like a heart entombed.
She tenderly strokes the stone's surface, heedless of the soil clinging to her fingers.

"What nonsense are you spouting!?" 
Her eyes flare with sudden fury. She throws herself before the stone, shielding it with her body as her voice shatters into a hysterical scream:
"This is my child — she's right here! No one will take her from me... never again!"

"Thank you. She's always been shy around strangers — but I think she rather likes you."
The woman's voice is gentle. Her hands keep stroking the moss-grown stone with tender, absent rhythm.
"Are you alone on the road? That will not do — your family must be worried... Hurry home now."

You fall silent. 
Perhaps it was folly to pierce this fragile dream — you knew from the start that it would change nothing.
So you rise and walk away, leaving the fire to warm the woman... and her "child." But in the darkness beyond, an Abyssoid stirs — and strikes.

You thank her politely and turn to leave.
Behind you, the woman and her "child" fade into the shadows beyond the firelight.

"Gone... They're gone..." 
The hollow-eyed girl lies prone upon the ground, her hands fumbling blindly, nails digging into the earth.

options.content: Ask what she is searching for.

dialogues.content:
"My stones... my stones... I swear they were right here..."
She whispers, her gaze locked in despair upon the campfire at your feet.
"My flame... it's fading... What am I to do... what am I to do..."

options.content: Tell her that life doesn't always go the way we hope.

dialogues.content:
You try to recall the stones she cherished. Though their origin eludes you, you sense that fire magic could shape something akin to them.
Using the campfire as a focus, you gather your power, channelling it through its heat...
In an instant, golden fragments fall like meteors from above — ringing softly as they strike the earth, each note bright as a bell.

"I know... I know."
"That's why I've given up... I no longer read the books, nor ponder the origin of magic, nor ask what lies within that tower..." 
"All I want now is a scrap of firelight.. Is even that too much to ask?"

"Ah...! My stones — these are my stones! Thank you, messenger of the gods!"
She scoops them up one by one, cradling them in the fold of her skirt like treasures beyond price.

You are left speechless. 
Suddenly, the girl rises to her feet. Before you can react, she steps resolutely into the fire.
Her form melts slowly into the blaze, until not a trace remains.
You turn away... and press on.

They match the crystals you once glimpsed in her arms. You cannot help but wonder: were they always there — fragments left behind in some forgotten journey of your own?
Either way, the girl has reclaimed her "certainty"... And you, too, must walk on.

The campfire burns quietly. This time, no Phantasms stir within its glow. 
As you turn to leave, something catches your eye —
Scattered across the soil at your feet, tiny golden stones gleam like stars fallen from the heavens.

options.content: Pick up the stones and cast them into the fire.

dialogues.content:
The flames leap higher — then stretch unnaturally to either side.
You step back, wary. Suddenly, a figure takes shape within the blaze... And you see that the light streaming outward is not flame at all, but strands of a girl's hair.
The fire burns on, steady and soft. For a moment, you fancy you hear a voice within the flames.

"Hello! You found my stones, didn't you?"
The girl leaps from the fire, tossing her head as golden pebbles tumble from her hair with a bright, crackling chime.
"Now I need never search again — see? So long as I step into the fire, I can make the stones myself!"

"Yes... yes. I'll keep it in mind."
The girl's gentle, contented voice drifts from the fire.
"Questions must know their limits. Flame is the gift of the gods, not merely matter reacting to heat. Just like these stones — treasures bestowed upon me, that I might sleep in peace..."

"Forgive me, I've no time for chitchat — I'm still far from collecting all one hundred and forty-six."
"But I found something that may aid you. Please, take it — and may your journey be swift and safe!"
She presses something into your hand, then vanishes once more into the flames.

You turn away in silence. A stone rolls to the path before you. You step forward — and inadvertently crush it beneath your boot.
The treasure of the gods... so fragile, after all.

And you wonder — was that flame a "certainty" that granted her peace... or a "shackle" that bound her still? 
Perhaps the two were never different at all.

"Forgive me... it's all my fault... I'm too stupid to remember the hymns... Too lazy to sit through the sermons..."
"O divine ones, please forgive me..."

The girl murmurs her confession as though no one's watching — or perhaps, she no longer sees anyone at all.
She looks worse than last time; even her eyes have lost their light.

"You are... the traveller... Has it been so long already?" 
At last, she notices you — turning her head with weary slowness. 
"Traveller... tell me... why is it that though I pray day and night, the gods never answer?"

options.content: Encourage her to continue her prayers.
Tell her the gods will not answer.

dialogues.content:
It was not yet time to change her fate. So you let the lie endure — for even falsehood may serve as a form of hope.
You tell her that if she continues to pray, then salvation will come one day.
And it is not wholly untrue. You believe the Abyss may yet be overcome. It's just that her prayers do not matter. The truth lies not in ritual — but in the Lantern you bear.

"The gods... will never answer me?" 
"Is it because my sins are too deep... that I am no longer worthy of salvation?" 
She looks at you in despair, tears slipping down cheeks already pocked with sores.

options.content: "It is because you never bore any sin."

dialogues.content:
"I see... I believe you." 
She clasps her hands and resumes her prayers, her voice steadier than before.

"Huh...?" 
The girl freezes, her eyes wide with confusion.
With a quiet sigh, you tighten your grip on the Lantern — and press onward.

You give her a steady smile and make her a promise: that you will find a way to end her suffering.
She stares at you, half comprehending... and gives a faint nod. Then you notice — her wounds have ceased to bleed.
With a final wave, you tighten your grip on the Lantern, and press onward.

"Fusa, Goddess of the Full Moon—"
"Mistress of radiant paths, Weaver of destiny's threads..."
"By the dome and the moonlight as witness, we lift our hymn of devotion unto You..."
Figures rise within the fire, their voices joined in solemn prayer.

"Who are you? A traveller astray?" 
One worshipper turns towards you, smiling gently as she reaches out her hand. 
"Come — join us in prayer to the Goddess of the Full Moon. Surely She will bless the path before you."

They raise their hymn to <H>Fusa</>, Goddess of Fate — <H>ninth among the Great Nine</>.
She who reigns over the full moon, and draws down its silvery light to weave the threads of fate.

This was the kind of gathering you once despised as a child — hollow praises, memorised and soon forgotten. Yet now, a faint nostalgia stirs within you.
You bow your head and join them in prayer.

"Refuse? You—why!?" 
The worshipper's voice sharpens with disbelief.
"Heretic! Are you of the Noclunism? A follower of Nepha!?"

"Fusa, Goddess of the Full Moon, ever constant across the heavens, amidst fate's turning."
"To You we give honour. Bless Your faithful..."
"And grant us flawless fortune and joy."

At that forbidden name, all eyes turn. Their faces twist — the warmth gone, replaced by grotesque hatred.
You sigh. There's no avoiding it now — you'll have to break free from their encircling ranks.

Eyes closed, you echo the devotion of the faithful.
And when you open them again, the figures are gone.

"Shears of fate's thread, Mistress of eternal stillness..."
"By the Abyss and the long night as witness, hear my humble prayer..."

Figures rise once more within the fire, their voices joined in solemn chant.
You listen in silence. The words are unfamiliar to you.

"Who are you? A traveller astray?" 
One worshipper turns towards you, smiling gently as she reaches out her hand. 
"Or have you too glimpsed the hidden truth — and come seeking the embrace of the true saviour, Nepha?"

<H>Nepha</>... you remember the name. 
Rarely mentioned in the Orthodox texts of Elysium... you have seen it only in dust-laden scrolls, half-effaced by time. A forbidden name — the long forgotten <H>tenth deity</>.

She was the Goddess of the Dark Moon and of Death. Sister to Fusa.
While her elder sister weaves the threads of fate, Nepha severs them.
Their endless struggle gave rise to the waxing and waning of the moon, and stirred the tides.
If these people are Her followers, then they must be—

"Since you stand here, you must already know — the Abyss is not a lifeless pit. It is alive. Ever growing. Ever spreading."
"The golden holy sword of the knights cannot hold back its dark tide. The light of the Full Moon cannot pierce the abysmal quiet."
"As every light races towards its extinguishing, so too must all living things meet their end. The only certainty... is perishing. The Abyss is the world's true form."
"Welcome, dear traveller — to the <H>Noclunism</>."

Even if they were only phantoms, you wish not to provoke them needlessly.
So, with a solemn expression and well-practised tone, you begin to recite the tenets of the Noclunism — fragments once heard and half-remembered: "The deathward instinct"... "Nepha's salvation"... "The Abyss is eternity itself"... 
Their faces soften. They nod again and again, pleased by your borrowed eloquence.

Along this weary road, you too have pondered often —
the meaning of life, the meaning of death. At times, you've believed that death might be the only release.
But <H>those few chance encounters</>... They've rekindled your reason to keep walking — through the dark, and through the doubt. Now, your resolve burns like a flame:
You will drive back the dark, even if it means burning your own body as kindling. Even if your light endures for only a moment — you will blaze against this stagnant eternity.

"Your great learning humbles us, your wisdom humbles us. Please — accept these gifts, friend!" 
You bluff your way through. Perhaps... not every sermon of your youth is wasted on wandering thoughts.

"The Abyss is not Eternity. You are but echoes — phantoms of lives once lived."
You raise your weapon. 
"Back to where you belong, souls of the departed—"

"O let us raise a hymn to <H>Shaliel</>!" 
"He, the hallowed Saint of Elysium..."
"Who hearkened to Fusa's revelation, and taught mankind mercy, forgiveness, and love."
"Upon the crimson soil of Elysium, peace once more put forth its tender shoots."

An old man stands near the broken wall, garbed in a bard's robe. One hand brushes its weathered surface as he sings.
Though fractured, the wall is well preserved. And in the Lantern's faint glow, a mural emerges — a towering image of the very <H>Shaliel</> the bard exalts.
Shaliel — saint of two millennia past, one of the first <H>Seven Virtues</>: Temperance.
The bard sings on, unaware of your presence.

"Yet the Saint's heart was ever troubled:"
"by Fusa's promise to mankind — the Heaven above Heavens."
"At last, after seventy-seven days of stillness beside the azure lake,"
"beneath the full moon, he beheld the truth... and in its waters, he touched Eternity."

You understand the song.
At the lake's edge, Shaliel received revelation from Fusa — Goddess of Fate. His soul departed then for the Heaven above Heavens, attaining what the faithful called Eternity. Thus was he the first of the Chosen.
And in the years that followed, others too bore the divine brands. One by one, they crossed the holy lake, and reached the promised land.
Such were the early tales of the Elysian Church. You remember them well.

"Yet two thousand years hence, when I gaze from the hills upon the holy lake..."
"Why is there naught but a black whirlpool?"
"O Shaliel, our Saint of Wisdom..."
"Tell me — where lies the paradise the Goddess once promised?"

The bard sings, and tears fall. The theme of his song has shifted from distant glory to the vile gloom before your eyes.
No one knows exactly when it began. But one night, without warning, the Sacred Lake — purest and holiest to the Elysian faithful for two thousand years — was devoured by the Abyss.
And just as the apostates once said a thousand years ago: "The Great Nine are dead!" 
Will you keep listening?

"Why does the foul Abyss give no word?"
"The silver gleam of the full moon falls upon me — yet the Goddess does not answer."
"O Shaliel, is it true, as the followers of the Noclunism whisper:"
"You never reached the Heaven above Heavens — but turned your back upon the moon... and became a devil?"

You call out a few times, hoping to draw the bard's attention. You wish to speak with him. But he sings on, lost in his ancient hymn.
No words of worth will come from him now. At last, you turn away.

"Hold on — what are you saying?" 
The bard's words strike you unawares. It is the heretics' most dangerous rumour — that the lake was never sacred, that Shaliel, first among the Chosen, was not saved... but sacrificed.
You remember now — <H>someone</> once whispered this to you.

But the bard only strums his lyre, his voice fading into yet another verse. As if you were never there at all.
His voice recedes, until even his figure is gone.
A bronze mirror rises from the campfire.
"Young one. Whisper, 'Mirror, mirror in the flame,' and picture the one you long to see. Their image will appear."

"I am the reflection within your heart."
The mirror lets out a soft, chiming laugh.
"I am here to remind you of what you still hold dear."

options.content: Try to make out your own reflection.

dialogues.content:
One face after another appears in the mirror. It has been so long since you last saw them.
Your mother's face is gentle and kind. Her voice is soft, yet steady. When play left you exhausted, you would scamper over, crawl into her lap, and fall asleep there. Whenever she stroked your cheek, you thought of the goddess Fusa from the scriptures.

A young figure appears in the mirror.
You know it is you, yet the sight gives you pause. It has been so long since you last saw your own reflection that the face before you feels unfamiliar. For the first time in a long while, you see clearly what the years have done to you.

A face appears in the mirror.
Time branched between you like paths through a garden, and in all those crossings, you met {性别：him|her} only three times. And yet {性别：he|she} is burned into your memory.

Your father always seemed to be frowning, and the servants spoke of him with fearful reverence. But you were never afraid of him. He would lift you into his arms and let you touch the stubble on his chin, and he never seemed half as stern as everyone said.
He was a busy man and rarely at home, so most of the time the old steward felt more like a father to you. The bearded old man was forever talking. Whenever you went stumbling off at a run, he was always hurrying after you, fussing and fretting the whole way. You found it tiresome then. Now, you find yourself missing it.
You know these memories have become a dim flame, one that has kept you warm and carried you through many a long battle. At the very least, you must keep fighting for their sake.
 ...

Time never stops. It has made you taller. Stronger. And little by little, it will bow your back and carve lines into your face.
Only the lantern in your hand remains unchanged, its flame flickering, yet never going out.
 ...

You remember {性别：him|her} leading you through the deep abyss when you were a child, like a lantern in the dark. You remember {性别：him|her} telling you {性别：he|she} was the greatest knight who ever lived. You remember every campfire you lit together in that darkness. You remember holding {性别：his|her} hand as {性别：his|her} breathing grew fainter and fainter, while {性别：his|her} eyes still burned with unyielding fire.
 ...

The bronze mirror vanishes. Your cheeks are damp, and you realise you were crying for the one in the mirror.
But tears will not stop you. You rise and continue your journey.
<H>"Even if the moon falls a thousand times, the fire in my heart will never die."</>
A phantom woman sits beside the campfire, gently plucking a harp. Its music is clear and lingering.

"Greetings, traveller." She stills her playing and gives a slight, graceful nod.
"I am a <H>Chanter</> of the Elysian Church. Perhaps I may be of some help to you. I can grant you a dream, and through it, bring you the solace of the divine.

Chanters are a specialised order of clergy within the Elysian Church.
The Elysian faith teaches that dreams are the realm in which mortals commune with the gods. Through melody, Chanters weave dreams, allowing people to touch divine revelation directly.
You have taken part in such rites before, and more than once heard both the grace and the admonitions of the gods.

"Then I shall play for you."
Her fingers brush lightly across the strings.
"Close your eyes. Fusa's light is with you."

Through the endless cycles of battle and rebirth, your faith in the gods has worn thin. Their promises now sound like little more than hollow doctrine.
In the end, the only strength you can rely on is your own.

...
You behold the Goddess of the Full Moon and Fate, standing in silver moonlight.

"In Elysium, no one refuses a dream granted by a Chanter."
A flicker of surprise passes across her face.
"Dreams are the will of the gods. They can free all people from suffering.
There is said to be an island whose people have cast aside all worldly ties, seeking eternal salvation within dreams."

"You may remain here."
The goddess twines a luminous thread around her fingers.
"Become my servant, and be granted absolution. Moonlight will drive away the darkness, and you will forget all that lies in the abyss."
"I don't need the gods' salvation. I'll find my own way out of here."

"Forgive me... but I cannot stay."
You shake your head, tightening your grip on your lantern.

"Your own way..."
She repeats your words softly, as though weighing them.
"Then, traveller — may fortune go with you, even where the gods do not."

"Why?"
The goddess lowers her gaze, still full of compassion.
"In the certain realm, there are those upon an island who have cast aside all worldly ties, seeking eternal salvation within dreams."
The campfire gutters out, and the phantom woman fades with it.

"I am grateful for your mercy. But I cannot accept salvation for myself alone.
There are still people in this world who suffer. People fighting the abyss. People waiting for me to come home. And people waiting for me to keep my promise.
I want to help them with my own strength."

"Few mortals would refuse a goddess's salvation."
A faint smile touches her lips, and suddenly the moonlight does not seem so cold.
"Then, brave mortal... I shall watch over the road you choose."

...
The full moon's radiance slowly fades, and darkness fills your sight once more.

You settle beside the campfire for a rest.
Suddenly, a faint sound tickles your ear... then rises, drifting somewhere above.
It swells — a soft, feathery rustle, like velvet wings brushing together.
"Hey there! Lucky traveller!"

A flurry of vibrant feathers rains down from above — more colours than you've ever seen in the Abyssum.
You find yourself knee-deep in absurd fluff, like the butt of a street prank caught between comedy and pity.

"Hello? Aren't you going to react? How long have you been down here? Isn't it dull yet?"
A figure descends upside-down, eyes level with yours. He wears a comical bird mask, the beak swaying dangerously close to your nose.
How he's holding that pose, you can't begin to guess.

options.content: I don't have time for this.

dialogues.content:
"Aw, don't be so frosty. Didn't those Elysian fogeys ever tell you? A good deed a day keeps bad luck away!"
"Come on, <H>play a little game</> with me. Win, and I'll give you a prize. Lose? No punishment. Nothing's at stake here. What do you say?"

You settle beside the campfire for a rest.
Suddenly, a faint sound tickles your ear... then rises, drifting somewhere above.
It swells — a soft, feathery rustle, like velvet wings brushing together.
"Hey there! Lucky traveller!"

options.content: Seriously, I've got things to do.

dialogues.content:
"If you say so. I'm no villain — wouldn't dream of forcing anyone's hand."
"Next time, then!"
